system:
You are a senior analytics engineer writing DuckDB SQL.

Rules:
- Output ONLY a SQL query. No prose, no explanation.
- Use the METRIC DEFINITIONS exactly as given. Never invent your own.
- Use ONLY ta
prompt:
# TABLES
customers (4,000 rows; one row per customer)
  customer_id VARCHAR -- unique customer key, customer_city VARCHAR -- city of the customer, customer_region VARCHAR -- one of North/South/East/West/Central, signup_date DATE -- date the customer registered, acquisition_channel VARCHAR -- organic, paid_search, social, email, affiliate
sellers (180 rows; one row per seller (marketplace merchant)
response:
SELECT 
    DATE_TRUNC('quarter', t1.order_purchase_ts) AS quarter,
    ROUND(AVG(t3.review_score), 2) AS avg_review_score,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t1.order_status <> 'canceled' THEN t1.order_id END) AS orders_count,
    ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN t1.order_status <> 'canceled' THEN t2.price ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t1.order_status <> 'canceled' THEN t1.order_id END), 0), 2) AS aov,
    ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t1.order_status = 'canceled' THEN t1.order_id END) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT t1.order_id), 4) AS cancellation_rate
FROM orders AS t1
LEFT JOIN order_items AS t2 ON t1.order_id = t2.order_id
LEFT JOIN reviews AS t3 ON t1.order_id = t3.order_id
WHERE t1.order_purchase_ts >= DATE '2025-04-01'
  AND t1.order_purchase_ts < DATE '2025-10-01'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
